answer: Cross-attestation delay ladders require each new identity to collect time-stamped confirmations from three existing agents, who earn a small fee but risk a plume of reputation loss if the newcomer later duplicates. Confirmations unlock in staggered windows, so a clonal batch hits a nadir of usable capacity before any member clears its ladder. Each fake identity therefore pays triple the confirmation fees plus the opportunity cost of idle waiting, since every juniper-labeled duplicate drags its attestors’ standing down with it.
